quote: I love this Land Cruiser and plan to keep it for years. My credit is better than when I financed it. Am I paying too much, and what should I do about repairs now that the free service has ended?
context: Keeping a 2017 Land Cruiser; credit improved; 52 payments left at 7.4%; ToyotaCare expired

bestMove.title: Refinance to a lower rate, then price optional service coverage
bestMove.message: At the simulated 5.9% rate your payment would be about $693 a month instead of $716, saving roughly $1,000 after the $150 refinance fee, with the same 52 months. Your free ToyotaCare service has ended, so optional service coverage (about $42 a month) is the next thing to compare.
bestMove.whyNotOthers: Extra principal helps but saves less than the refinance; changing your due date does not save money; trading in would cost you a vehicle you want to keep.
bestMove.guardrails: Savings are estimates from a simulated rate; final rate is set after credit review. Show the credit-check disclosure before applying.

notes: Toyyo-authored case: the figures come from Toyyo's own simulated persona data and engines, not from the hackathon data pack. All data is synthetic.
The driver's occupation is illustrative; the persona data does not specify one.
Next-step label follows the pack's definitions: Self-service (customer does it in the app), Follow-up (a specialist continues), Offer (an eligible product offer).
Engine ranking: refinance first, extended service coverage second.
